GPUBindingResource: A resource accepted by a bind group entry, such as a sampler, texture view, buffer binding, or external texture.
GPUBuffer: A GPUBuffer represents a block of memory that can be used in GPU operations. Data is stored in linear layout, meaning that each byte of the allocation can be addressed by its offset from the start of the GPUBuffer, subject to alignment restrictions depending on the operation. Some GPUBuffers can be mapped which makes the block of memory accessible via an ArrayBuffer called its mapping.
GPUBuffer#size: The length of the GPUBuffer allocation in bytes.
GPUBuffer#usage: The allowed usages for this GPUBuffer.
GPUBuffer#mapState: The buffer is not mapped for use by this.getMappedRange(). A mapping of the buffer has been requested, but is pending. It may succeed, or fail validation in mapAsync().
GPUBuffer#unmap(): Unmaps the mapped range of the GPUBuffer and makes its contents available for use by the GPU again.
GPUBufferBinding: A buffer resource and the byte range exposed to a shader through a bind group.
GPUBufferBinding#offset: The offset, in bytes, from the beginning of buffer to the beginning of the range exposed to the shader by the buffer binding.
GPUBufferBinding#size: The size, in bytes, of the buffer binding. If not provided, specifies the range starting at offset and ending at the end of buffer.
GPUSampler: A GPUSampler encodes transformations and filtering information that can be used in a shader to interpret texture resource data.
GPUTexture: A texture is made up of 1d, 2d, or 3d arrays of data which can contain multiple values per-element to represent things like colors. Textures can be read and written in many ways, depending on the GPUTextureUsage they are created with. For example, textures can be sampled, read, and written from render and compute pipeline shaders, and they can be written by render pass outputs. Internally, textures are often stored in GPU memory with a layout optimized for multidimensional access rather than linear access.
GPUTexture#depthOrArrayLayers: The depth or layer count of this GPUTexture.
GPUTexture#mipLevelCount: The number of mip levels of this GPUTexture.
GPUTexture#sampleCount: The number of sample count of this GPUTexture.
GPUTexture#dimension: The dimension of the set of texel for each of this GPUTexture’s subresources.
GPUTexture#usage: The allowed usages for this GPUTexture.
GPUTexture#createView(descriptor):
Creates a GPUTextureView.

@param descriptor Description of the GPUTextureView to create.
GPUTextureView: A GPUTextureView is a view onto some subset of the texture subresources defined by a particular GPUTexture.
GPUColor: An RGBA color represented by four components.
GPUOrigin2D: A two-dimensional origin represented by x and y coordinates.
GPUOrigin2D#x: The X coordinate of the origin; defaults to 0 when the origin is specified as a dictionary.
GPUOrigin2D#y: The Y coordinate of the origin; defaults to 0 when the origin is specified as a dictionary.
GPUOrigin3D: A three-dimensional origin represented by x, y, and z coordinates.
GPUOrigin3D#x: The X coordinate of the origin; defaults to 0 when the origin is specified as a dictionary.
GPUOrigin3D#y: The Y coordinate of the origin; defaults to 0 when the origin is specified as a dictionary.
GPUOrigin3D#z: The Z coordinate of the origin; defaults to 0 when the origin is specified as a dictionary.
GPUExtent3D: A three-dimensional extent represented by width, height, and depth or array-layer count.
GPUExtent3D#depthOrArrayLayers: The depth of the extent or the number of array layers it contains. If used with a GPUTexture with a GPUTextureDimension of "3d" defines the depth of the texture. If used with a GPUTexture with a GPUTextureDimension of "2d" defines the number of array layers in the texture.
GPUObjectBase: Common properties included by WebGPU objects. Its label can identify the object in diagnostics and developer tools.
GPUObjectBase#label: A developer-provided label which is used in an implementation-defined way. It can be used by the browser, OS, or other tools to help identify the underlying internal object to the developer. Examples include displaying the label in GPUError messages, console warnings, browser developer tools, and platform debugging utilities.
GPUSupportedLimits: GPUSupportedLimits exposes an adapter or device’s supported limits. See GPUAdapter.limits and GPUDevice.limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxTextureDimension1D: The maximum allowed value for the size.width of a texture created with dimension "1d".
GPUSupportedLimits#maxTextureDimension2D: The maximum allowed value for the size.width and size.height of a texture created with dimension "2d".
GPUSupportedLimits#maxTextureDimension3D: The maximum allowed value for the size.width, size.height and size.depthOrArrayLayers of a texture created with dimension "3d".
GPUSupportedLimits#maxTextureArrayLayers: The maximum allowed value for the size.depthOrArrayLayers of a texture created with dimension "2d".
GPUSupportedLimits#maxBindGroups: The maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayouts allowed in bindGroupLayouts when creating a GPUPipelineLayout.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxBindGroupsPlusVert: The maximum number of bind group and vertex buffer slots used simultaneously, counting any empty slots below the highest index. Validated in createRenderPipeline() and in draw calls.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxImmediateSize: The maximum size, in bytes, of immediate data range used in a pipeline. Note: 64 bytes is the size of a 4×4 matrix of f32 values.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxBindingsPerBindGro: The number of binding indices available when creating a GPUBindGroupLayout. Note: This limit is normative, but arbitrary. With the default binding slot limits, it is impossible to use 1000 bindings in one bind group, but this allows GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry.binding values up to 999. This limit allows implementations to treat binding space as an array, within reasonable memory space, rather than a sparse map structure.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxDynamicUniformBuff: The maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are uniform buffers with dynamic offsets. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxDynamicStorageBuff: The maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage buffers with dynamic offsets. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxSampledTexturesPer: For each possible GPUShaderStage stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are sampled textures. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxSamplersPerShaderS: For each possible GPUShaderStage stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are samplers. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageBuffersPerS: For each possible GPUShaderStage stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage buffers. See Exceeds the binding slot limits. Note: This limit applies to all stages. At device initialization, it is normalized with maxStorageBuffersInVertexStage and maxStorageBuffersInFragmentStage so that in the validation algorithm, each stage can be checked against just one of the three limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageBuffersInVe: For the vertex stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage buffers. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageBuffersInFr: For the fragment stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage buffers. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageTexturesPer: For each possible GPUShaderStage stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage textures. See Exceeds the binding slot limits. Note: This limit applies to all stages. At device initialization, it is normalized with maxStorageTexturesInVertexStage and maxStorageTexturesInFragmentStage so that in the validation algorithm, each stage can be checked against just one of the three limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageTexturesInV: For the vertex stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage textures. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageTexturesInF: For the fragment stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are storage textures. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxUniformBuffersPerS: For each possible GPUShaderStage stage, the maximum number of GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entries across a GPUPipelineLayout which are uniform buffers. See Exceeds the binding slot limits.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxUniformBufferBindi: The maximum GPUBufferBinding.size for bindings with a GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entry for which entry.buffer?.type is "uniform".
GPUSupportedLimits#maxStorageBufferBindi: The maximum GPUBufferBinding.size for bindings with a GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entry for which entry.buffer?.type is "storage" or "read-only-storage".
GPUSupportedLimits#minUniformBufferOffse: The required alignment for GPUBufferBinding.offset and the dynamic offsets provided in setBindGroup(), for bindings with a GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entry for which entry.buffer?.type is "uniform".
GPUSupportedLimits#minStorageBufferOffse: The required alignment for GPUBufferBinding.offset and the dynamic offsets provided in setBindGroup(), for bindings with a GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry entry for which entry.buffer?.type is "storage" or "read-only-storage".
GPUSupportedLimits#maxVertexBuffers: The maximum number of buffers when creating a GPURenderPipeline.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxBufferSize: The maximum size of size when creating a GPUBuffer.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxVertexAttributes: The maximum number of attributes in total across buffers when creating a GPURenderPipeline.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxVertexBufferArrayS: The maximum allowed arrayStride when creating a GPURenderPipeline.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxInterStageShaderVa: The maximum allowed number of input or output variables for inter-stage communication (like vertex outputs or fragment inputs).
GPUSupportedLimits#maxColorAttachments: The maximum allowed number of color attachments in GPURenderPipelineDescriptor.fragment.targets, GPURenderPassDescriptor.colorAttachments, and GPURenderPassLayout.colorFormats.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxColorAttachmentByt: The maximum number of bytes necessary to hold one sample (pixel or subpixel) of render pipeline output data, across all color attachments.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxComputeWorkgroupSt: The maximum number of bytes of workgroup storage used for a compute stage GPUShaderModule entry-point.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxComputeInvocations: The maximum value of the product of the workgroup_size dimensions for a compute stage GPUShaderModule entry-point.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxComputeWorkgroupSi: The maximum value of the workgroup_size X dimension for a compute stage GPUShaderModule entry-point.
The maximum value of the workgroup_size Y dimensions for a compute stage GPUShaderModule entry-point.
The maximum value of the workgroup_size Z dimensions for a compute stage GPUShaderModule entry-point.
GPUSupportedLimits#maxComputeWorkgroupsP: The maximum value for the arguments of dispatchWorkgroups(workgroupCountX, workgroupCountY, workgroupCountZ).
GPUAdapterInfo: GPUAdapterInfo exposes various identifying information about an adapter.
GPUAdapterInfo#vendor: The name of the vendor of the adapter, if available. Empty string otherwise.
GPUAdapterInfo#architecture: The name of the family or class of GPUs the adapter belongs to, if available. Empty string otherwise.
GPUAdapterInfo#device: A vendor-specific identifier for the adapter, if available. Empty string otherwise. Note: This is a value that represents the type of adapter. For example, it may be a PCI device ID. It does not uniquely identify a given piece of hardware like a serial number.
GPUAdapterInfo#description: A human readable string describing the adapter as reported by the driver, if available. Empty string otherwise. Note: Because no formatting is applied to description attempting to parse this value is not recommended. Applications which change their behavior based on the GPUAdapterInfo, such as applying workarounds for known driver issues, should rely on the other fields when possible.
GPUAdapterInfo#subgroupMinSize: If the "subgroups" feature is supported, the minimum supported subgroup size for the adapter.
GPUAdapterInfo#subgroupMaxSize: If the "subgroups" feature is supported, the maximum supported subgroup size for the adapter.
GPUAdapterInfo#isFallbackAdapter: Whether the adapter is a fallback adapter.

GPUDevice#adapterInfo: Information about the physical adapter which created the device that this GPUDevice refers to. For a given GPUDevice, the GPUAdapterInfo values exposed are constant over time.

GPUBindGroupLayout: A GPUBindGroupLayout defines the interface between a set of resources bound in a GPUBindGroup and their accessibility in shader stages.
GPUBindGroup: A GPUBindGroup defines a set of resources to be bound together in a group and how the resources are used in shader stages.
GPUPipelineLayout: A GPUPipelineLayout defines the mapping between resources of all GPUBindGroup objects set up during command encoding in setBindGroup(), and the shaders of the pipeline set by GPURenderCommandsMixin.setPipeline or GPUComputePassEncoder.setPipeline.
GPUShaderModule: Contains shader code compiled for use in GPU pipelines.
GPUShaderModule#getCompilationInfo(): Returns any messages generated during the GPUShaderModule’s compilation. The locations, order, and contents of messages are implementation-defined. In particular, messages aren’t necessarily ordered by lineNum.
GPUCompilationMessage: A GPUCompilationMessage is an informational, warning, or error message generated by the GPUShaderModule compiler. The messages are intended to be human readable to help developers diagnose issues with their shader code. Each message may correspond to a single point or range of the shader source, or may be unassociated with any specific part of the code.
GPUCompilationMessage#message: The human-readable, localizable text for this compilation message. Note: The message should follow the best practices for language and direction information. This includes making use of any future standards which may emerge regarding the reporting of string language and direction metadata.
GPUCompilationMessage#type: The severity level of the message. If the type is "error", it corresponds to a shader-creation error.
GPUCompilationMessage#lineNum: The line number in the shader code the message corresponds to. Value is one-based, such that a lineNum of 1 indicates the first line of the shader code. Lines are delimited by line breaks. If the message corresponds to a substring this points to the line on which the substring begins. Must be 0 if the message does not correspond to any specific point in the shader code.
GPUCompilationMessage#linePos: The offset, in UTF-16 code units, from the beginning of line lineNum of the shader code to the point or beginning of the substring that the message corresponds to. Value is one-based, such that a linePos of 1 indicates the first code unit of the line. If message corresponds to a substring this points to the first UTF-16 code unit of the substring. Must be 0 if the message does not correspond to any specific point in the shader code.
GPUCompilationMessage#offset: The offset from the beginning of the shader code in UTF-16 code units to the point or beginning of the substring that message corresponds to. Must reference the same position as lineNum and linePos. Must be 0 if the message does not correspond to any specific point in the shader code.
GPUCompilationMessage#length: The number of UTF-16 code units in the substring that message corresponds to. If the message does not correspond with a substring then length must be 0.
GPUCompilationInfo: Contains the messages produced while compiling a GPUShaderModule.
GPUCompilationInfo#messages: Compilation messages, including errors, warnings, and informational messages.

GPUQueue: Submits command buffers and schedules writes and copies for execution by the GPUDevice.
GPUQueue#submit(commandBuffers): Schedules the execution of the command buffers by the GPU on this queue. Submitted command buffers cannot be used again.

GPUQuerySet: Stores the results of a configured kind and count of GPU queries.
GPUQuerySet#type: The type of the queries managed by this GPUQuerySet.
GPUQuerySet#count: The number of queries managed by this GPUQuerySet.
GPUDeviceLostInfo: Information resolved by GPUDevice.lost when the device is lost, including the reason and diagnostic message.
GPUDeviceLostInfo#reason: Reason reported for the device loss.
GPUDeviceLostInfo#message: Implementation-provided diagnostic message describing the device loss.
GPUError: GPUError is the base interface for all errors surfaced from popErrorScope() and the uncapturederror event.
GPUError#message: A human-readable, localizable text message providing information about the error that occurred. Note: This message is generally intended for application developers to debug their applications and capture information for debug reports, not to be surfaced to end-users.
GPUValidationError: GPUValidationError is a subtype of GPUError which indicates that an operation did not satisfy all validation requirements. Validation errors are always indicative of an application error, and is expected to fail the same way across all devices assuming the same [[features]] and [[limits]] are in use.
GPUOutOfMemoryError: GPUOutOfMemoryError is a subtype of GPUError which indicates that there was not enough free memory to complete the requested operation. The operation may succeed if attempted again with a lower memory requirement (like using smaller texture dimensions), or if memory used by other resources is released first.
GPUInternalError: GPUInternalError is a subtype of GPUError which indicates than an operation failed for a system or implementation-specific reason even when all validation requirements have been satisfied. For example, the operation may exceed the capabilities of the implementation in a way not easily captured by the supported limits. The same operation may succeed on other devices or under difference circumstances.
GPUObjectDescriptorBase: Common label field shared by descriptors that create WebGPU objects.
GPURequestAdapterOptions: Options that constrain which GPU adapter is selected.
GPURequestAdapterOptions#featureLevel: Requests an adapter that supports at least a particular set of capabilities. This influences the [[default feature level]] of devices created from this adapter. The capabilities for each level are defined below, and the exact steps are defined in requestAdapter() and "a new device". If the implementation or system does not support all of the capabilities in the requested feature level, requestAdapter() will return null.
GPURequestAdapterOptions#powerPreference: Optionally provides a hint indicating what class of adapter should be selected from the system’s available adapters. The value of this hint may influence which adapter is chosen, but it must not influence whether an adapter is returned or not.
GPURequestAdapterOptions#forceFallbackAd: When set to true indicates that only a fallback adapter may be returned. If the user agent does not support a fallback adapter, will cause requestAdapter() to resolve to null. Note: requestAdapter() may still return a fallback adapter if forceFallbackAdapter is set to false and either no other appropriate adapter is available or the user agent chooses to return a fallback adapter. Developers that wish to prevent their applications from running on fallback adapters should check the info.isFallbackAdapter attribute prior to requesting a GPUDevice.
GPURequestAdapterOptions#xrCompatible: When set to true indicates that the best adapter for rendering to a WebXR session must be returned. If the user agent or system does not support WebXR sessions then adapter selection may ignore this value. Note: If xrCompatible is not set to true when the adapter is requested, GPUDevices created from the adapter cannot be used to render for WebXR sessions.
GPUDeviceDescriptor#requiredFeatures: Specifies the features that are required by the device request. The request will fail if the adapter cannot provide these features. Exactly the specified set of features, and no more or less, will be allowed in validation of API calls on the resulting device.
GPUDeviceDescriptor#requiredLimits: Specifies the limits that are required by the device request. The request will fail if the adapter cannot provide these limits. Each key with a non-undefined value must be the name of a member of supported limits.
GPUDeviceDescriptor#defaultQueue: The descriptor for the default GPUQueue.
GPUDeviceDescriptor#onUncapturedError: Callback invoked for errors that are not captured by an error scope.
GPUBufferDescriptor: Describes a GPUBuffer's size, usage, and optional mapped-at-creation state.
GPUBufferDescriptor#size: The size of the buffer in bytes.
GPUBufferDescriptor#usage: The allowed usages for the buffer.
GPUBufferDescriptor#mappedAtCreation: If true creates the buffer in an already mapped state, allowing getMappedRange() to be called immediately. It is valid to set mappedAtCreation to true even if usage does not contain MAP_READ or MAP_WRITE. This can be used to set the buffer’s initial data. Guarantees that even if the buffer creation eventually fails, it will still appear as if the mapped range can be written/read to until it is unmapped.
GPUTextureDescriptor: Describes a GPUTexture's size, format, usage, and optional view formats.
GPUTextureDescriptor#size: The width, height, and depth or layer count of the texture.
GPUTextureDescriptor#mipLevelCount: The number of mip levels the texture will contain.
GPUTextureDescriptor#sampleCount: The sample count of the texture. A sampleCount > 1 indicates a multisampled texture.
GPUTextureDescriptor#dimension: Whether the texture is one-dimensional, an array of two-dimensional layers, or three-dimensional.
GPUTextureDescriptor#usage: The allowed usages for the texture.
GPUTextureDescriptor#viewFormats: Specifies what view format values will be allowed when calling createView() on this texture (in addition to the texture’s actual format). Formats in this list must be texture view format compatible with the texture format.
GPUTextureDescriptor#textureBindingViewD: On devices with "core-features-and-limits", this is ignored, and there is no such restriction.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor: Describes the format, dimension, mip levels, array layers, and aspect of a GPUTextureView.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#format: The format of the texture view. Must be either the format of the texture or one of the viewFormats specified during its creation.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#dimension: The dimension to view the texture as.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#usage: The allowed usage(s) for the texture view. Must be a subset of the usage flags of the texture. If 0, defaults to the full set of usage flags of the texture. Note: If the view’s format doesn’t support all of the texture’s usages, the default will fail, and the view’s usage must be specified explicitly.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#aspect: Which aspect(s) of the texture are accessible to the texture view.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#baseMipLevel: The first (most detailed) mipmap level accessible to the texture view.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#mipLevelCount: How many mipmap levels, starting with baseMipLevel, are accessible to the texture view.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#baseArrayLayer: The index of the first array layer accessible to the texture view.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#arrayLayerCount: How many array layers, starting with baseArrayLayer, are accessible to the texture view.
GPUTextureViewDescriptor#swizzle: A string of length four, with each character mapping to the texture view’s red/green/blue/alpha channels, respectively. "r": Take its value from the red channel of the texture.
GPUSamplerDescriptor: Describes the address modes, filtering modes, and level-of-detail limits for a GPUSampler.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#addressModeU: Specifies the address modes for the texture width, height, and depth coordinates, respectively.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#addressModeV: Specifies the address modes for the texture width, height, and depth coordinates, respectively.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#addressModeW: Specifies the address modes for the texture width, height, and depth coordinates, respectively.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#magFilter: Specifies the sampling behavior when the sampled area is smaller than or equal to one texel.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#minFilter: Specifies the sampling behavior when the sampled area is larger than one texel.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#mipmapFilter: Specifies behavior for sampling between mipmap levels.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#lodMinClamp: Specifies the minimum and maximum levels of detail, respectively, used internally when sampling a texture.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#lodMaxClamp: Specifies the minimum and maximum levels of detail, respectively, used internally when sampling a texture.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#compare: When provided the sampler will be a comparison sampler with the specified GPUCompareFunction. Note: Comparison samplers may use filtering, but the sampling results will be implementation-dependent and may differ from the normal filtering rules.
GPUSamplerDescriptor#maxAnisotropy: Specifies the maximum anisotropy value clamp used by the sampler. Anisotropic filtering is enabled when maxAnisotropy is > 1 and the implementation supports it. Anisotropic filtering improves the image quality of textures sampled at oblique viewing angles. Higher maxAnisotropy values indicate the maximum ratio of anisotropy supported when filtering.
GPUBindGroupLayoutDescriptor: Describes the entries that define a GPUBindGroupLayout.
GPUBindGroupLayoutDescriptor#entries: A list of entries describing the shader resource bindings for a bind group.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry: Describes one binding's index, shader visibility, and resource-specific layout.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry#binding: A unique identifier for a resource binding within the GPUBindGroupLayout, corresponding to a GPUBindGroupEntry.binding and a @binding attribute in the GPUShaderModule.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry#visibility: A bitset of the members of GPUShaderStage. Each set bit indicates that a GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry’s resource will be accessible from the associated shader stage.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry#buffer: Exactly one of these members must be set, indicating the binding type. The contents of the member specify options specific to that type. The corresponding resource in createBindGroup() requires the corresponding binding resource type for this binding.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry#sampler: Exactly one of these members must be set, indicating the binding type. The contents of the member specify options specific to that type. The corresponding resource in createBindGroup() requires the corresponding binding resource type for this binding.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry#texture: Exactly one of these members must be set, indicating the binding type. The contents of the member specify options specific to that type. The corresponding resource in createBindGroup() requires the corresponding binding resource type for this binding.
GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry#storageTexture: Exactly one of these members must be set, indicating the binding type. The contents of the member specify options specific to that type. The corresponding resource in createBindGroup() requires the corresponding binding resource type for this binding.
GPUBufferBindingLayout: Describes the type, dynamic-offset behavior, and minimum size of a buffer binding.
GPUBufferBindingLayout#type: Indicates the type required for buffers bound to this binding.
GPUBufferBindingLayout#hasDynamicOffset: Indicates whether this binding requires a dynamic offset.
GPUBufferBindingLayout#minBindingSize: Indicates the minimum size of a buffer binding used with this bind point. Bindings are always validated against this size in createBindGroup().
GPUSamplerBindingLayout: Describes the sampler binding type expected by a shader.
GPUSamplerBindingLayout#type: Indicates the required type of a sampler bound to this binding.
GPUTextureBindingLayout: Describes the sample type, view dimension, and multisampling of a texture binding.
GPUTextureBindingLayout#sampleType: Indicates the type required for texture views bound to this binding.
GPUTextureBindingLayout#viewDimension: Indicates the required dimension for texture views bound to this binding.
GPUTextureBindingLayout#multisampled: Indicates whether or not texture views bound to this binding must be multisampled.
GPUStorageTextureBindingLayout: Describes the access mode, format, and view dimension of a storage texture binding.
GPUStorageTextureBindingLayout#access: The access mode for this binding, indicating readability and writability.
GPUStorageTextureBindingLayout#format: The required format of texture views bound to this binding.
GPUStorageTextureBindingLayout#viewDimen: Indicates the required dimension for texture views bound to this binding.
GPUBindGroupDescriptor: Describes the layout and resources used to create a GPUBindGroup.
GPUBindGroupDescriptor#layout: The GPUBindGroupLayout the entries of this bind group will conform to.
GPUBindGroupDescriptor#entries: A list of entries describing the resources to expose to the shader for each binding described by the layout.
GPUBindGroupEntry: Associates a binding index with the GPU resource supplied for that binding.
GPUBindGroupEntry#binding: A unique identifier for a resource binding within the GPUBindGroup, corresponding to a GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry.binding and a @binding attribute in the GPUShaderModule.
GPUBindGroupEntry#resource: The resource to bind, which may be a GPUSampler, GPUTexture, GPUTextureView, GPUBuffer, GPUBufferBinding, or GPUExternalTexture.
GPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor: Lists the GPUBindGroupLayouts used by a pipeline.
GPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor#bindGroupLay: A list of optional GPUBindGroupLayouts the pipeline will use. Each element corresponds to a @group attribute in the GPUShaderModule, with the Nth element corresponding with @group(N).
GPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor#immediateSiz: The size, in bytes, of the immediate data range used by the pipeline.
GPUShaderModuleDescriptor: Describes the shader code and compilation options used to create a GPUShaderModule.
GPUShaderModuleDescriptor#code: The WGSL source code for the shader module.
GPUShaderModuleDescriptor#compilationHin: A list of GPUShaderModuleCompilationHints. Any hint provided by an application should contain information about one entry point of a pipeline that will eventually be created from the entry point.
GPUShaderModuleCompilationHint: A hint associating a shader entry point with the pipeline layout expected to use it.
GPUShaderModuleCompilationHint#entryPoin: Name of the shader entry point associated with this compilation hint.
GPUShaderModuleCompilationHint#layout: A GPUPipelineLayout that the GPUShaderModule may be used with in a future createComputePipeline() or createRenderPipeline() call. If set to "auto" the layout will be the default pipeline layout for the entry point associated with this hint will be used.
GPUPipelineDescriptorBase: Common label field shared by render and compute pipeline descriptors.
GPUPipelineDescriptorBase#layout: The GPUPipelineLayout for this pipeline, or "auto" to generate the pipeline layout automatically. Note: If "auto" is used the pipeline cannot share GPUBindGroups with any other pipelines.
GPUProgrammableStage: A GPUProgrammableStage describes the entry point in the user-provided GPUShaderModule that controls one of the programmable stages of a pipeline. Entry point names follow the rules defined in WGSL identifier comparison.
GPUProgrammableStage#module: The GPUShaderModule containing the code that this programmable stage will execute.
GPUProgrammableStage#entryPoint: The name of the function in module that this stage will use to perform its work. NOTE: Since the entryPoint dictionary member is not required, methods which consume a GPUProgrammableStage must use the "get the entry point" algorithm to determine which entry point it refers to.
GPUProgrammableStage#constants: Specifies the values of pipeline-overridable constants in the shader module module. Each such pipeline-overridable constant is uniquely identified by a single pipeline-overridable constant identifier string, representing the pipeline constant ID of the constant if its declaration specifies one, and otherwise the constant’s identifier name.
GPUComputePipelineDescriptor: Describes the layout and compute shader stage used to create a GPUComputePipeline.
GPUComputePipelineDescriptor#compute: Describes the compute shader entry point of the pipeline.
GPURenderPipelineDescriptor: Describes the layout and programmable stages and fixed-function state of a GPURenderPipeline.
GPURenderPipelineDescriptor#vertex: Describes the vertex shader entry point of the pipeline and its input buffer layouts.
GPURenderPipelineDescriptor#primitive: Describes the primitive-related properties of the pipeline.
GPURenderPipelineDescriptor#depthStencil: Describes the optional depth-stencil properties, including the testing, operations, and bias.
GPURenderPipelineDescriptor#multisample: Describes the multi-sampling properties of the pipeline.
GPURenderPipelineDescriptor#fragment: Describes the fragment shader entry point of the pipeline and its output colors. If not provided, the § 23.2.8 No Color Output mode is enabled.
GPUPrimitiveState: Describes primitive topology, strip format, front face, and culling for a render pipeline.
GPUPrimitiveState#topology: The type of primitive to be constructed from the vertex inputs.
GPUPrimitiveState#stripIndexFormat: For pipelines with strip topologies ("line-strip" or "triangle-strip"), this determines the index buffer format and primitive restart value ("uint16"/0xFFFF or "uint32"/0xFFFFFFFF). It is not allowed on pipelines with non-strip topologies. Note: Some implementations require knowledge of the primitive restart value to compile pipeline state objects.
GPUPrimitiveState#frontFace: Defines which polygons are considered front-facing.
GPUPrimitiveState#cullMode: Defines which polygon orientation will be culled, if any.
GPUPrimitiveState#unclippedDepth: If true, indicates that depth clipping is disabled. Requires the "depth-clip-control" feature to be enabled.
GPUMultisampleState: Describes sample count, sample mask, and alpha-to-coverage behavior.
GPUMultisampleState#count: Number of samples per pixel. This GPURenderPipeline will be compatible only with attachment textures (colorAttachments and depthStencilAttachment) with matching sampleCounts.
GPUMultisampleState#mask: Mask determining which samples are written to.
GPUMultisampleState#alphaToCoverageEnabl: When true indicates that a fragment’s alpha channel should be used to generate a sample coverage mask.
GPUFragmentState: Describes the fragment shader stage and its color targets.
GPUFragmentState#targets: A list of GPUColorTargetState defining the formats and behaviors of the color targets this pipeline writes to.
GPUColorTargetState: Describes the format, write mask, and optional blending for a fragment color target.
GPUColorTargetState#format: The GPUTextureFormat of this color target. The pipeline will only be compatible with GPURenderPassEncoders which use a GPUTextureView of this format in the corresponding color attachment.
GPUColorTargetState#blend: The blending behavior for this color target. If left undefined, disables blending for this color target.
GPUColorTargetState#writeMask: Bitmask controlling which channels are are written to when drawing to this color target.
GPUBlendState: Describes the color and alpha blend components applied to a color target.
GPUBlendState#color: Defines the blending behavior of the corresponding render target for color channels.
GPUBlendState#alpha: Defines the blending behavior of the corresponding render target for the alpha channel.
GPUBlendComponent: Describes one color or alpha blend component's operation and factors.
GPUBlendComponent#operation: Defines the GPUBlendOperation used to calculate the values written to the target attachment components.
GPUBlendComponent#srcFactor: Defines the GPUBlendFactor operation to be performed on values from the fragment shader.
GPUBlendComponent#dstFactor: Defines the GPUBlendFactor operation to be performed on values from the target attachment.
GPUDepthStencilState: Describes depth testing, stencil testing, and depth bias for a render pipeline.
GPUDepthStencilState#format: The format of depthStencilAttachment this GPURenderPipeline will be compatible with.
GPUDepthStencilState#depthWriteEnabled: Indicates if this GPURenderPipeline can modify depthStencilAttachment depth values.
GPUDepthStencilState#depthCompare: The comparison operation used to test fragment depths against depthStencilAttachment depth values.
GPUDepthStencilState#stencilFront: Defines how stencil comparisons and operations are performed for front-facing primitives.
GPUDepthStencilState#stencilBack: Defines how stencil comparisons and operations are performed for back-facing primitives.
GPUDepthStencilState#stencilReadMask: Bitmask controlling which depthStencilAttachment stencil value bits are read when performing stencil comparison tests.
GPUDepthStencilState#stencilWriteMask: Bitmask controlling which depthStencilAttachment stencil value bits are written to when performing stencil operations.
GPUDepthStencilState#depthBias: Constant depth bias added to each triangle fragment. See biased fragment depth for details.
GPUDepthStencilState#depthBiasSlopeScale: Depth bias that scales with the triangle fragment’s slope. See biased fragment depth for details.
GPUDepthStencilState#depthBiasClamp: The maximum depth bias of a triangle fragment. See biased fragment depth for details.
GPUStencilFaceState: Describes stencil comparison and the operations applied to a stencil face.
GPUStencilFaceState#compare: The GPUCompareFunction used when testing the [[stencilReference]] value against the fragment’s depthStencilAttachment stencil values.
GPUStencilFaceState#failOp: The GPUStencilOperation performed if the fragment stencil comparison test described by compare fails.
GPUStencilFaceState#depthFailOp: The GPUStencilOperation performed if the fragment depth comparison described by depthCompare fails.
GPUStencilFaceState#passOp: The GPUStencilOperation performed if the fragment stencil comparison test described by compare passes.
GPUVertexState: Describes the vertex shader stage and vertex buffer layouts for a render pipeline.
GPUVertexState#buffers: A list of GPUVertexBufferLayouts, each defining the layout of vertex attribute data in a vertex buffer used by this pipeline.
GPUVertexBufferLayout: Describes the stride, step mode, and attributes of a vertex buffer.
GPUVertexBufferLayout#arrayStride: The stride, in bytes, between elements of this array.
GPUVertexBufferLayout#stepMode: Whether each element of this array represents per-vertex data or per-instance data
GPUVertexBufferLayout#attributes: An array defining the layout of the vertex attributes within each element.
GPUVertexAttribute: Describes one vertex attribute's format and byte offset in a vertex buffer.
GPUVertexAttribute#offset: The offset, in bytes, from the beginning of the element to the data for the attribute.
GPUVertexAttribute#shaderLocation: The numeric location associated with this attribute, which will correspond with a "@location" attribute declared in the vertex.module.
GPUTexelCopyBufferLayout: "GPUTexelCopyBufferLayout" describes the "layout" of texels in a "buffer" of bytes (GPUBuffer or AllowSharedBufferSource) in a "texel copy" operation.
GPUTexelCopyBufferLayout#offset: The offset, in bytes, from the beginning of the texel data source (such as a GPUTexelCopyBufferInfo.buffer) to the start of the texel data within that source.
GPUTexelCopyBufferLayout#bytesPerRow: The stride, in bytes, between the beginning of each texel block row and the subsequent texel block row. Required if there are multiple texel block rows (i.e. the copy height or depth is more than one block).
GPUTexelCopyBufferLayout#rowsPerImage: Number of texel block rows per single texel image of the texture. rowsPerImage × bytesPerRow is the stride, in bytes, between the beginning of each texel image of data and the subsequent texel image. Required if there are multiple texel images (i.e. the copy depth is more than one).
GPUTexelCopyBufferInfo: "GPUTexelCopyBufferInfo" describes the "info" (GPUBuffer and GPUTexelCopyBufferLayout) about a "buffer" source or destination of a "texel copy" operation. Together with the copySize, it describes the footprint of a region of texels in a GPUBuffer.
GPUTexelCopyBufferInfo#buffer: A buffer which either contains texel data to be copied or will store the texel data being copied, depending on the method it is being passed to.
GPUTexelCopyTextureInfo: "GPUTexelCopyTextureInfo" describes the "info" (GPUTexture, etc.) about a "texture" source or destination of a "texel copy" operation. Together with the copySize, it describes a sub-region of a texture (spanning one or more contiguous texture subresources at the same mip-map level).
GPUTexelCopyTextureInfo#mipLevel: Mip-map level of the texture to copy to/from.
GPUTexelCopyTextureInfo#origin: Defines the origin of the copy - the minimum corner of the texture sub-region to copy to/from. Together with copySize, defines the full copy sub-region.
GPUTexelCopyTextureInfo#aspect: Defines which aspects of the texture to copy to/from.
GPUCommandBufferDescriptor: Options used when finishing a GPUCommandEncoder to create a GPUCommandBuffer.
GPUCommandEncoderDescriptor: Options used to create a GPUCommandEncoder.
GPUComputePassTimestampWrites: Selects query slots for compute-pass beginning and end timestamps.
GPUComputePassTimestampWrites#querySet: The GPUQuerySet, of type "timestamp", that the query results will be written to.
GPUComputePassTimestampWrites#beginningO: If defined, indicates the query index in querySet into which the timestamp at the beginning of the compute pass will be written.
GPUComputePassTimestampWrites#endOfPassW: If defined, indicates the query index in querySet into which the timestamp at the end of the compute pass will be written.
GPUComputePassDescriptor: Options for beginning a compute pass, including optional timestamp writes.
GPUComputePassDescriptor#timestampWrites: Defines which timestamp values will be written for this pass, and where to write them to.
GPURenderPassTimestampWrites: Selects query slots for render-pass beginning, end, and optional per-stage timestamps.
GPURenderPassTimestampWrites#querySet: The GPUQuerySet, of type "timestamp", that the query results will be written to.
GPURenderPassTimestampWrites#beginningOf: If defined, indicates the query index in querySet into which the timestamp at the beginning of the render pass will be written.
GPURenderPassTimestampWrites#endOfPassWr: If defined, indicates the query index in querySet into which the timestamp at the end of the render pass will be written.
GPURenderPassDescriptor: Describes the color, depth/stencil, and optional timestamp attachments for a render pass.
GPURenderPassDescriptor#colorAttachments: The set of GPURenderPassColorAttachment values in this sequence defines which color attachments will be output to when executing this render pass. Due to usage compatibility, no color attachment may alias another attachment or any resource used inside the render pass.
GPURenderPassDescriptor#depthStencilAtta: The GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment value that defines the depth/stencil attachment that will be output to and tested against when executing this render pass. Due to usage compatibility, no writable depth/stencil attachment may alias another attachment or any resource used inside the render pass.
GPURenderPassDescriptor#occlusionQuerySe: The GPUQuerySet value defines where the occlusion query results will be stored for this pass.
GPURenderPassDescriptor#timestampWrites: Defines which timestamp values will be written for this pass, and where to write them to.
GPURenderPassDescriptor#maxDrawCount: The maximum number of draw calls that will be done in the render pass. Used by some implementations to size work injected before the render pass. Keeping the default value is a good default, unless it is known that more draw calls will be done.
GPURenderPassColorAttachment: Describes a color attachment and its load, store, and resolve operations for a render pass.
GPURenderPassColorAttachment#view: Describes the texture subresource that will be output to for this color attachment. The subresource is determined by calling get as texture view(view).
GPURenderPassColorAttachment#depthSlice: Indicates the depth slice index of "3d" view that will be output to for this color attachment.
GPURenderPassColorAttachment#resolveTarg: Describes the texture subresource that will receive the resolved output for this color attachment if view is multisampled. The subresource is determined by calling get as texture view(resolveTarget).
GPURenderPassColorAttachment#clearValue: Indicates the value to clear view to prior to executing the render pass. If not provided, defaults to {r: 0, g: 0, b: 0, a: 0}. Ignored if loadOp is not "clear". The components of clearValue are all double values. They are converted to a texel value of texture format matching the render attachment. If conversion fails, a validation error is generated.
GPURenderPassColorAttachment#loadOp: Indicates the load operation to perform on view prior to executing the render pass. Note: It is recommended to prefer clearing; see "clear" for details.
GPURenderPassColorAttachment#storeOp: The store operation to perform on view after executing the render pass.
GPUTextureOrGPUTextureView: A value that is either a GPUTexture or a GPUTextureView.
GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment: Describes the depth and stencil operations for a render pass attachment.
GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment#view: Describes the texture subresource that will be output to and read from for this depth/stencil attachment. The subresource is determined by calling get as texture view(view).
GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment#dept: Indicates the value to clear view’s depth component to prior to executing the render pass. Ignored if depthLoadOp is not "clear". Must be between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive.
Indicates the load operation to perform on view’s depth component prior to executing the render pass. Note: It is recommended to prefer clearing; see "clear" for details.
The store operation to perform on view’s depth component after executing the render pass.
Indicates that the depth component of view is read only.
GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment#sten: Indicates the value to clear view’s stencil component to prior to executing the render pass. Ignored if stencilLoadOp is not "clear". The value will be converted to the type of the stencil aspect of view by taking the same number of LSBs as the number of bits in the stencil aspect of one texel of view.
Indicates the load operation to perform on view’s stencil component prior to executing the render pass. Note: It is recommended to prefer clearing; see "clear" for details.
The store operation to perform on view’s stencil component after executing the render pass.
Indicates that the stencil component of view is read only.
GPURenderPassLayout: Describes the attachment formats and sample count used by a render pass or render bundle.
GPURenderPassLayout#colorFormats: A list of the GPUTextureFormats of the color attachments for this pass or bundle.
GPURenderPassLayout#depthStencilFormat: The GPUTextureFormat of the depth/stencil attachment for this pass or bundle.
GPURenderPassLayout#sampleCount: Number of samples per pixel in the attachments for this pass or bundle.
GPURenderBundleDescriptor: Options used when finishing a GPURenderBundleEncoder to create a GPURenderBundle.
GPURenderBundleEncoderDescriptor: Options used to create a GPURenderBundleEncoder.
GPURenderBundleEncoderDescriptor#depthRe: If true, indicates that the render bundle does not modify the depth component of the GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment of any render pass the render bundle is executed in. See read-only depth-stencil.
GPURenderBundleEncoderDescriptor#stencil: If true, indicates that the render bundle does not modify the stencil component of the GPURenderPassDepthStencilAttachment of any render pass the render bundle is executed in. See read-only depth-stencil.
GPUQuerySetDescriptor: Describes the query type and number of queries in a GPUQuerySet.
GPUQuerySetDescriptor#type: The type of queries managed by GPUQuerySet.
GPUQuerySetDescriptor#count: The number of queries managed by GPUQuerySet.
GPUUncapturedErrorCallback: Callback invoked when a GPUDevice reports an error that is not captured by an error scope.
GPUAddressMode: Selects how texture coordinates outside the normalized range are addressed.
GPUAddressMode#\tClampToEdge: Texture coordinates are clamped between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive.
GPUAddressMode#\tRepeat: Texture coordinates wrap to the other side of the texture.
GPUAddressMode#\tMirrorRepeat: Texture coordinates wrap to the other side of the texture, but the texture is flipped when the integer part of the coordinate is odd.
GPUBlendFactor: Defines the source or destination factor used to scale color and alpha values during blending.
GPUBlendFactor#\tSrc: Uses the value (Rsrc, Gsrc, Bsrc, Asrc).
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusSrc: Uses the value (1 - Rsrc, 1 - Gsrc, 1 - Bsrc, 1 - Asrc).
GPUBlendFactor#\tSrcAlpha: Uses the value (Asrc, Asrc, Asrc, Asrc).
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusSrcAlpha: Uses the value (1 - Asrc, 1 - Asrc, 1 - Asrc, 1 - Asrc).
GPUBlendFactor#\tDst: Uses the value (Rdst, Gdst, Bdst, Adst).
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusDst: Uses the value (1 - Rdst, 1 - Gdst, 1 - Bdst, 1 - Adst).
GPUBlendFactor#\tDstAlpha: Uses the value (Adst, Adst, Adst, Adst).
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusDstAlpha: Uses the value (1 - Adst, 1 - Adst, 1 - Adst, 1 - Adst).
GPUBlendFactor#\tSrcAlphaSaturated: Uses the value (min(Asrc, 1 - Adst), min(Asrc, 1 - Adst), min(Asrc, 1 - Adst), 1).
GPUBlendFactor#\tConstant: Uses the value (Rconst, Gconst, Bconst, Aconst).
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusConstant: Uses the value (1 - Rconst, 1 - Gconst, 1 - Bconst, 1 - Aconst).
GPUBlendFactor#\tSrc1: Uses the value (Rsrc1, Gsrc1, Bsrc1, Asrc1), dual-source-blending.
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusSrc1: Uses the value (1 - Rsrc1, 1 - Gsrc1, 1 - Bsrc1, 1 - Asrc1).
GPUBlendFactor#\tSrc1Alpha: Uses the value (Asrc1, Asrc1, Asrc1, Asrc1).
GPUBlendFactor#\tOneMinusSrc1Alpha: Uses the value (1 - Asrc1, 1 - Asrc1, 1 - Asrc1, 1 - Asrc1).
GPUBlendOperation: Defines the operation used to combine source and destination blend factors.
GPUBlendOperation#\tAdd: Uses the value RGBAsrc × RGBAsrcFactor + RGBAdst × RGBAdstFactor.
GPUBlendOperation#\tSubtract: Uses the value RGBAsrc × RGBAsrcFactor - RGBAdst × RGBAdstFactor.
GPUBlendOperation#\tReverseSubtract: Uses the value RGBAdst × RGBAdstFactor - RGBAsrc × RGBAsrcFactor.
GPUBufferBindingType: Selects how a buffer binding is accessed by shaders.
GPUBufferBindingType#\tBindingNotUsed: Declares that this binding is not used by the pipeline.
GPUBufferBindingType#\tUniform: The buffer is accessed as a uniform buffer.
GPUBufferBindingType#\tStorage: The buffer is accessed as a read-write storage buffer.
GPUBufferBindingType#\tReadOnlyStorage: The buffer is accessed as a read-only storage buffer.
GPUBufferMapState: The mapping state of a GPUBuffer: mapped or unmapped.
GPUBufferMapState#\tUnmapped: The buffer is not mapped for use by this.getMappedRange().
GPUBufferMapState#\tPending: A mapping of the buffer has been requested, but is pending. It may succeed, or fail validation in mapAsync().
GPUBufferMapState#\tMapped: The buffer is mapped and this.getMappedRange() may be used.
GPUCompareFunction: Selects the comparison operation used by depth and stencil tests.
GPUCompareFunction#\tLess: A provided value passes the comparison test if it is less than the sampled value.
GPUCompareFunction#\tEqual: A provided value passes the comparison test if it is equal to the sampled value.
GPUCompareFunction#\tLessEqual: A provided value passes the comparison test if it is less than or equal to the sampled value.
GPUCompareFunction#\tGreater: A provided value passes the comparison test if it is greater than the sampled value.
GPUCompareFunction#\tNotEqual: A provided value passes the comparison test if it is not equal to the sampled value.
GPUCompareFunction#\tGreaterEqual: A provided value passes the comparison test if it is greater than or equal to the sampled value.
GPUCompilationMessageType: Classifies a GPUCompilationMessage as an error, warning, or informational message.
GPUCompilationMessageType#\tError: Classifies a compilation message as an error, warning, or informational message.
GPUCompilationMessageType#\tWarning: Classifies a compilation message as an error, warning, or informational message.
GPUCompilationMessageType#\tInfo: Classifies a compilation message as an error, warning, or informational message.
GPUCullMode: Selects whether no polygons, front-facing polygons, or back-facing polygons are culled.
GPUDeviceLostReason: Indicates why a GPUDevice was lost.
GPUDeviceLostReason#\tUnknown: The device was lost for a reason other than an explicit destroy request.
GPUDeviceLostReason#\tDestroyed: The device was lost because GPUDevice.destroy() was called.
GPUErrorFilter: Selects the error category captured by a GPUDevice error scope.
GPUErrorFilter#\tValidation: Indicates that the error scope will catch a GPUValidationError.
GPUErrorFilter#\tOutOfMemory: Indicates that the error scope will catch a GPUOutOfMemoryError.
GPUErrorFilter#\tInternal: Indicates that the error scope will catch a GPUInternalError.
GPUFeatureName: Each GPUFeatureName identifies a set of functionality which, if available, allows additional usages of WebGPU that would have otherwise been invalid.
GPUFeatureName#\tCoreFeaturesAndLimits: The "core-features-and-limits" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tDepthClipControl: Allows depth clipping to be disabled.
GPUFeatureName#\tDepth32FloatStencil8: The "depth32-float-stencil8" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureCompressionBC: Allows for explicit creation of textures of BC compressed formats which include the "S3TC", "RGTC", and "BPTC" formats. Note: This feature only supports 2D textures. If 3D textures are needed, use "texture-compression-bc-sliced-3d".
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureCompressionBCSli: The "texture-compression-bcsliced3-d" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureCompressionETC2: Allows for explicit creation of textures of ETC2 compressed formats. Note: This feature only supports 2D textures.
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureCompressionASTC: Allows for explicit creation of textures of ASTC compressed formats. Note: This feature only supports 2D textures. If 3D textures are needed, use "texture-compression-astc-sliced-3d".
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureCompressionASTCS: The "texture-compression-astcsliced3-d" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tTimestampQuery: Adds the ability to query timestamps from GPU command buffers. See § 20.4 Timestamp Query.
GPUFeatureName#\tIndirectFirstInstance: Allows the use of non-zero firstInstance values in indirect draw parameters and indirect drawIndexed parameters.
GPUFeatureName#\tShaderF16: Allows the use of the half-precision floating-point type f16 in WGSL.
GPUFeatureName#\tRG11B10UfloatRenderable: The "rg11-b10-ufloat-renderable" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tBGRA8UnormStorage: The "bgra8-unorm-storage" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tFloat32Filterable: The "float32-filterable" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tFloat32Blendable: The "float32-blendable" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tClipDistances: Allows the use of clip_distances in WGSL.
GPUFeatureName#\tDualSourceBlending: Allows the use of blend_src in WGSL and simultaneously using both pixel shader outputs (@blend_src(0) and @blend_src(1)) as inputs to a blending operation with the single color attachment at location 0.
GPUFeatureName#\tSubgroups: Allows the use of the subgroup and quad operations in WGSL. The following entries of GPUAdapterInfo expose real values whenever the feature is available on the adapter: subgroupMinSize subgroupMaxSize
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureFormatsTier1: The "texture-formats-tier1" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tTextureFormatsTier2: The "texture-formats-tier2" optional feature name, used to check adapter support and request the feature when creating a device.
GPUFeatureName#\tPrimitiveIndex: Allows the use of primitive_index in WGSL.

GPUFilterMode: Selects the filtering behavior used for minification and magnification sampling.
GPUFilterMode#\tNearest: Return the value of the texel nearest to the texture coordinates.
GPUFilterMode#\tLinear: Select two texels in each dimension and return a linear interpolation between their values.
GPUFrontFace: Selects whether clockwise or counter-clockwise polygons are treated as front-facing.
GPUFrontFace#\tCCW: Polygons with vertices whose framebuffer coordinates are given in counter-clockwise order are considered front-facing.
GPUFrontFace#\tCW: Polygons with vertices whose framebuffer coordinates are given in clockwise order are considered front-facing.
GPUIndexFormat: The index format determines both the data type of index values in a buffer and, when used with strip primitive topologies ("line-strip" or "triangle-strip") also specifies the primitive restart value. The primitive restart value indicates which index value indicates that a new primitive should be started rather than continuing to construct the triangle strip with the prior indexed vertices.
GPULoadOp: Selects whether a render pass clears an attachment or loads its existing contents.
GPULoadOp#\tLoad: Loads the existing value for this attachment into the render pass.
GPULoadOp#\tClear: Loads a clear value for this attachment into the render pass. Note: On some GPU hardware (primarily mobile), "clear" is significantly cheaper because it avoids loading data from main memory into tile-local memory. On other GPU hardware, there isn’t a significant difference. As a result, it is recommended to use "clear" rather than "load" in cases where the initial value doesn’t matter (e.g. the render target will be cleared using a skybox).
GPUMipmapFilterMode: Selects how samples are filtered between mip levels.
GPUPowerPreference: Hints whether adapter selection should favor lower power use or higher performance.
GPUPowerPreference#\tLowPower: Indicates a request to prioritize power savings over performance. Note: Generally, content should use this if it is unlikely to be constrained by drawing performance; for example, if it renders only one frame per second, draws only relatively simple geometry with simple shaders, or uses a small HTML canvas element. Developers are encouraged to use this value if their content allows, since it may significantly improve battery life on portable devices.
GPUPowerPreference#\tHighPerformance: Indicates a request to prioritize performance over power consumption. Note: By choosing this value, developers should be aware that, for devices created on the resulting adapter, user agents are more likely to force device loss, in order to save power by switching to a lower-power adapter. Developers are encouraged to only specify this value if they believe it is absolutely necessary, since it may significantly decrease battery life on portable devices.
GPUPrimitiveTopology: Selects how vertex data is assembled into points, lines, or triangles.
GPUPrimitiveTopology#\tPointList: Each vertex defines a point primitive.
GPUPrimitiveTopology#\tLineList: Each consecutive pair of two vertices defines a line primitive.
GPUPrimitiveTopology#\tLineStrip: Each vertex after the first defines a line primitive between it and the previous vertex.
GPUPrimitiveTopology#\tTriangleList: Each consecutive triplet of three vertices defines a triangle primitive.
GPUPrimitiveTopology#\tTriangleStrip: Each vertex after the first two defines a triangle primitive between it and the previous two vertices.
GPUQueryType: Selects the kind of result recorded by a GPUQuerySet.
GPUQueryType#\tOcclusion: Records whether any samples pass the fragment tests for a render pass.
GPUQueryType#\tTimestamp: Records a GPU timestamp at a query location.
GPUSamplerBindingType: Selects the sampling operations supported by a sampler binding.
GPUSamplerBindingType#\tBindingNotUsed: Declares that this binding is not used by the pipeline.
GPUStencilOperation: Selects the operation applied to stencil values when a stencil test succeeds or fails.
GPUStencilOperation#\tIncrementClamp: Increments the current stencil value, clamping to the maximum representable value of the depthStencilAttachment’s stencil aspect.
GPUStencilOperation#\tDecrementClamp: Decrement the current stencil value, clamping to 0.
GPUStencilOperation#\tIncrementWrap: Increments the current stencil value, wrapping to zero if the value exceeds the maximum representable value of the depthStencilAttachment’s stencil aspect.
GPUStencilOperation#\tDecrementWrap: Decrement the current stencil value, wrapping to the maximum representable value of the depthStencilAttachment’s stencil aspect if the value goes below 0.
GPUStorageTextureAccess: Selects how a storage texture binding may be accessed by shaders.
GPUStorageTextureAccess#\tBindingNotUsed: Declares that this binding is not used by the pipeline.
GPUStorageTextureAccess#\tWriteOnly: Shaders may write to this storage texture.
GPUStorageTextureAccess#\tReadOnly: Shaders may read from this storage texture.
GPUStorageTextureAccess#\tReadWrite: Shaders may read from and write to this storage texture.
GPUStoreOp: Selects whether a render pass stores or discards an attachment's contents when the pass ends.
GPUStoreOp#\tStore: Stores the resulting value of the render pass for this attachment.
GPUStoreOp#\tDiscard: Discards the resulting value of the render pass for this attachment. Note: Discarded attachments behave as if they are cleared to zero, but implementations are not required to perform a clear at the end of the render pass. Implementations which do not explicitly clear discarded attachments at the end of a pass must lazily clear them prior to the reading the attachment contents, which occurs via sampling, copies, attaching to a later render pass with "load", displaying or reading back the canvas (get a copy of the image contents of a context), etc.
GPUTextureAspect: Selects which aspect of a texture is addressed, such as color, depth, stencil, or all aspects.
GPUTextureAspect#\tAll: All available aspects of the texture format will be accessible to the texture view. For color formats the color aspect will be accessible. For combined depth-stencil formats both the depth and stencil aspects will be accessible. Depth-or-stencil formats with a single aspect will only make that aspect accessible. The set of aspects is [color, depth, stencil].
GPUTextureAspect#\tStencilOnly: Only the stencil aspect of a depth-or-stencil format format will be accessible to the texture view. The set of aspects is [stencil].
GPUTextureAspect#\tDepthOnly: Only the depth aspect of a depth-or-stencil format format will be accessible to the texture view. The set of aspects is [depth].
